title: WHERE THE SIN OFFERING IS SLAUGHTERED

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The LORD said to Moses, 'Say to Aaron and his sons: "These are the regulations for the sin offering: The sin offering is to be slaughtered before the LORD in the place the burnt offering is slaughtered; it is most holy."'" - Lev 6:24-25 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The sin offering is slaughtered in the same place as the burnt offering — and then God calls it most holy.

Pause on that. The offering brought because someone failed is designated most holy. Not shameful. Not second-class. Most holy.

That runs against every instinct we have. We tend to think of confession as the embarrassing part of the Christian life, the thing we do quietly before getting on with the respectable business of worship and service. God ranks it among the holiest things that happened at His altar.

Why? Because dealing honestly with sin according to God's provision is one of the most God-honouring things a person can do. It takes His holiness seriously. It takes His mercy seriously. It refuses pretence.

The Pharisee in Jesus' parable listed his achievements. The tax collector could not lift his eyes and simply said, God, have mercy on me, a sinner. Jesus said it was the tax collector who went home justified (Lk 18:13-14).

If you have been putting off coming to God because of something you have done, understand what you are avoiding. Not a humiliating errand. The holiest ground available to you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I see confession as shameful rather than holy?
2. What am I avoiding bringing to God, and what would it mean to bring it today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that the place where I deal with my sin is holy ground before You. I come there now, honestly. Amen.
